title: customer-tokenflow-anomaly-triage-and-staged-stabilization
creator: Aisha Ramos
description:
Summary: A strategic enterprise customer (multi-tenant Dedicated deployment + hosted fallback) reported a sudden degradation in first-token time (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec drop across multiple model variants starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Symptoms: elevated TTFT, increased tail latency, and reduced token emission rates (25-60% loss depending on context window). Initial hypotheses: kernel selection heuristic misclassification under mixed short/long context workloads, KV-prefetch contention, and router priority inversion.

Actions taken so far:
- 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC: Customer report received via priority support channel; on-call engaged.
- 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC: Production traces pulled; identified correlation with recent kernel-selector rollout (selector v3) and a pattern of heterogeneous context windows (~15% short sessions mixed with long-generative sessions).
- 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: Repro harness created to simulate mixed fanout across hosted/dedicated; reproduced TTFT spike locally and in staging with same binary.
- 2026-03-10 07:00 UTC: Implemented temporary per-customer rate shaping and downgraded traffic for heavy long-context flows to prevent cascade; immediate customer relief observed (median TTFT improved from 820ms to 310ms).
- 2026-03-11 10:00 UTC: Prepared a rollback candidate that reverts kernel-selector heuristics to the previous stable logic (selector v2), plus a mitigation patch that disables aggressive KV-prefetch for sessions flagged as mixed-length.
- 2026-03-12 21:00 UTC: Canary rollout to 3% of affected fleet completed for selector-v2 rollback; monitoring shows stable TTFT and tokens/sec recovery on canary nodes.

Decision and trade-offs:
- Rolling back to selector-v2 reduces throughput for some well-behaved homogeneous long-context workloads (by ~8%) but stabilizes TTFT and prevents token starvation for mixed workloads. We prioritized customer SLAs over the modest throughput regression.
- Prefetch-disable mitigation reduces speculative memory pressure but may increase cold-start penalty on pure long-gen flows; acceptable short term.

Remaining work and owners:
- Full cluster rollback plan and cutover schedule (Owner: Jonah Kim) — target 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC for gradual ramp to 100% with canary monitoring windows.
- Post-rollback follow-up: refine kernel-selector telemetry to include context distribution and session fingerprints (Owner: Lina Patel).
- Long-term: redesign selector to be context-aware with lightweight runtime signals and a fallback cost-estimator (Owner: Runtime Team lead: Marco Silva).
- Customer communication: Drafted incident message and mitigation summary for CSM handoff (Owner: Aisha Ramos).

Links and artifacts: Incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/INC-207531, PR for rollback: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1842, Repro harness: https://ci.redwood/repro/207531, Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/latency/ttft-207531
acceptance_criteria: Median TTFT for affected customers returns to pre-incident baseline within 30% during the 48h window after full rollout
Sustained tokens/sec for mixed-context workloads improves to within 10% of baseline on production telemetry
Postmortem with root cause, timeline, and a concrete plan to prevent recurrence published and reviewed by runtime and platform teams
